claims.text: Combinatorial synthesis coupled with high-throughput micro-mechanical testing can reveal systematic mechanical-property variations as elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr are adjusted.
A standard or equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr composition can serve as the baseline alloy.
The percentages of one or more elements can be varied systematically while remaining within the HfNbTaTiZr alloy system.
The proposed comparisons should be performed at ambient temperature and typical strain rates.
Changing elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr modifies lattice distortion.
Changing elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr modifies phase distribution and grain-boundary characteristics.
Microstructural changes in HfNbTaTiZr can be associated with changes in hardness.
Lattice distortion, phase distribution, and grain-boundary characteristics mediate dislocation movement and plastic deformation.
Changing constituent percentages alters solid-solution strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion affect dislocation mobility and phase stability.
Composition-driven changes in dislocation mobility and phase stability produce changes in yield strength, ductility, and hardness.
Mechanical properties will exhibit measurable trends correlated with specific elemental-percentage changes.
The direction and magnitude of each property change depend on the identity and role of the element being varied.
HfNbTaTiZr processing can produce incomplete densification, cracking, or brittleness under some powder-metallurgy routes.
Extreme compositional variations may induce unwanted intermetallic phases or significant density and processing problems.
Nanoindentation and micro-tensile testing can be used as high-throughput micro-mechanical measurements across the composition library.
SEM or TEM characterization can measure grain size and phase distributions across the composition library.
A lack of statistically significant property variation correlated with composition, beyond experimental error, would falsify the proposed composition-property relationship.
